risks.note: Listed as a key risk in MD&A Risks & Concerns and as a weakness for both the Engineering and Tea Divisions. The shortage constrained Tea estate development, productivity initiatives and operational efficiency; management states adequate working capital support is critical to stabilise operations, pay wages and statutory dues on time and reduce reliance on high-cost borrowings, and flags that constraints in working capital and bank support may restrict business growth.
risks.risk: Working capital shortage and limited fund-based / non-fund-based banking support

risks.note: MD&A names aging manufacturing infrastructure as a key risk and states continuous technology upgradation remains essential to meet evolving customer requirements. The Engineering Division cites aging machinery affecting productivity and manufacturing efficiency; the Electrical Division cites constrained manufacturing, assembly, testing and expansion capacity creating production bottlenecks that reduce throughput and affect timely order fulfilment.
risks.risk: Aging manufacturing infrastructure and need for continuous technology upgradation

risks.note: MD&A lists intense market competition as a key risk. The Electrical Division has limited market share in a highly competitive transformer industry and faces pricing pressure from unorganised and low-cost competitors; the Engineering Division faces private-sector manufacturers with aggressive pricing; the Tea Division faces small tea growers and low-cost producers.
risks.risk: Intense competition and resulting margin pressure

risks.note: MD&A flags volatility in steel and other raw material prices as a key risk. The Electrical Division specifically cites copper, oil and steel price volatility, and the Engineering Division cites raw material price volatility impacting margins.

MD&A names dependence on capital expenditure trends in core sectors such as power, steel, cement and mining as a key risk; the Engineering Division adds that an economic slowdown or a reduction in industrial capex/modernisation may affect order inflow.
risks.risk: Dependence on capital expenditure cycles in core customer sectors

risks.note: Crop yield and quality depend on climatic conditions; FY 2025-26 saw adverse weather and pest infestation contributing to a production decline, and climate change and unpredictable weather patterns are listed as a threat. Tea production fell to 61.95 lakh kg from about 71.18 lakh kg.
risks.risk: Climate and weather dependence in the Tea Division

risks.note: Rising labour and input costs and labour shortages during the peak harvesting season hurt the Tea Division; escalating wage and operating costs are a listed threat and a high fixed manpower cost structure contributed to the production decline. Industrial relations remained cordial except in a few tea gardens in West Bengal and Assam, where there was occasional worker agitation over delayed wage and salary payments. The Engineering Division separately cites scarcity of skilled workmen and technical manpower and higher dependence on outsourced resources during peak workloads. A strike at the Electrical Division unit caused execution delays that led to a liquidated-damages provision.
risks.risk: Labour availability, wage cost escalation and industrial relations

risks.note: Exposure to tea price volatility and market fluctuations is a listed threat; subdued realisations and market volatility pressured revenue and profitability, while international trade disruption from geopolitical tensions and the West Asia crisis raised freight, logistics, insurance and input costs and affected export demand. Global economic uncertainties impacting export demand and realisations are also flagged.
risks.risk: Tea price volatility and weak realisations, with export demand exposure

currentContext.expansion: The AR discloses no new plant, line or greenfield expansion project and no commissioning or ramp timeline; capital spending in FY 2025-26 was maintenance and modernisation of existing facilities across the three divisions. In the Engineering Division at Kalyani the Company installed a 315 KW VFD with motor and a CNC cutting machine, replaced the Shed 6 roof with colour-coated galvalume sheet, replaced damaged brick flooring with paver-block flooring in the Shed 1 paint shop and Shed 5, and procured advanced design software through capital expenditure to strengthen design capability. The shortage constrained Tea estate development, productivity initiatives and operational efficiency; management states adequate working capital support is critical to stabilise operations, pay wages and statutory dues on time and reduce reliance on high-cost borrowings, and flags that constraints in working capital and bank support may restrict business growth.
- MD&A names aging manufacturing infrastructure as a key risk and states continuous technology upgradation remains essential to meet evolving customer requirements. The Engineering Division cites aging machinery affecting productivity and manufacturing efficiency; the Electrical Division cites constrained manufacturing, assembly, testing and expansion capacity creating production bottlenecks that reduce throughput and affect timely order fulfilment.
- MD&A lists intense market competition as a key risk. The Electrical Division has limited market share in a highly competitive transformer industry and faces pricing pressure from unorganised and low-cost competitors; the Engineering Division faces private-sector manufacturers with aggressive pricing; the Tea Division faces small tea growers and low-cost producers.
- MD&A flags volatility in steel and other raw material prices as a key risk. The Electrical Division specifically cites copper, oil and steel price volatility, and the Engineering Division cites raw material price volatility impacting margins.
- MD&A names dependence on capital expenditure trends in core sectors such as power, steel, cement and mining as a key risk; the Engineering Division adds that an economic slowdown or a reduction in industrial capex/modernisation may affect order inflow.
- Crop yield and quality depend on climatic conditions; FY 2025-26 saw adverse weather and pest infestation contributing to a production decline, and climate change and unpredictable weather patterns are listed as a threat. Tea production fell to 61.95 lakh kg from about 71.18 lakh kg.
- Rising labour and input costs and labour shortages during the peak harvesting season hurt the Tea Division; escalating wage and operating costs are a listed threat and a high fixed manpower cost structure contributed to the production decline. Industrial relations remained cordial except in a few tea gardens in West Bengal and Assam, where there was occasional worker agitation over delayed wage and salary payments. The Engineering Division separately cites scarcity of skilled workmen and technical manpower and higher dependence on outsourced resources during peak workloads. A strike at the Electrical Division unit caused execution delays that led to a liquidated-damages provision.
- Exposure to tea price volatility and market fluctuations is a listed threat; subdued realisations and market volatility pressured revenue and profitability, while international trade disruption from geopolitical tensions and the West Asia crisis raised freight, logistics, insurance and input costs and affected export demand. Global economic uncertainties impacting export demand and realisations are also flagged.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Electrical Division: focus on operational efficiency, quality improvement, timely project execution and market expansion to strengthen competitive position, including expanding the customer base across multiple states (Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, West Bengal)
- Engineering Division: technology upgradation, operational excellence, product innovation and market expansion, backed by adoption of advanced design software procured through capital expenditure
- Engineering Division: customer diversification - five new customers added during FY 2025-26 across steel, ferro alloy, mining …
